Subject: Cross-border governance request — DPA deviation and subprocessor attestations

Hi Aditya / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a few compliance items before we can finalise the SOW. Two specific asks from legal/security:

1) Halcyon has a temporary analytics partner in Canada that will process pseudonymised telemetry for a short pilot. We need confirmation that Redwood's DPA + UK Addendum/SCCs/TIA approach will cover a limited transient processor in Canada without a separate local addendum. Is there a narrow exception path?

2) Procurement wants signed attestation from any subprocessor who will touch EU personal data (even transiently). Can Redwood provide a per-subprocessor attestation template and a cadence for returning these?

I've attached our transfer questionnaire (halcyon-data-transfer-questionnaire.xlsx) and included procurement on the thread for timeline clarity — they need a yes/no on the exception by next Thursday so our internal sign-off stays on track.

Appreciate any clarity you can provide.

Best,
Emma

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear asks and the questionnaire.

Short answer: we can support the pilot without needing a separate local addendum for that transient processor, provided the processing falls within our documented safeguards and we obtain the requested subprocessor attestations.

What we'll need from Halcyon to proceed:
- A brief description of the telemetry fields (pseudonymised vs personal identifiers) — a row in the questionnaire is fine.
- Confirmation of pilot dates and an estimated volume of records.

Internal note: cc’ing Kimberly (Legal) and Laura (Security) to confirm the exception path and to provide the attestation template.

Planned next steps from Redwood:
1) Kimberly will confirm whether SCCs + UK IDTA + our standard TIA mapping suffice for the scenario.
2) We will provide a one-page subprocessor attestation template and a timeline for return (typical turnaround: 5–7 business days).
3) If any control gaps are identified, we will propose compensating measures (logging retention controls, contract-side SCAs).

I attached a short excerpt of our DPA for quick reference (redwood-dpa-excerpt.pdf). Happy to hop on a 30-min call early next week if that helps.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Thanks — procurement wants to be explicit on the timeline: sign-off is targeted for the week of Nov 9. For our legal team to greenlight, we need confirmation that:

• The Canadian partner will not be persistent controller of any identifiable EU subject; processing is limited to pseudonymised telemetry only.
• Redwood can provide a signed attestation from that partner (or confirm Redwood will secure it on Halcyon’s behalf).

If Redwood can commit to collecting the attestation and producing it to Halcyon within 7 business days of receiving the partner contact, procurement will mark the DPA deviation request as acceptable pending review.

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Halcyon — DPA deviation assessment and attestation template

Aditya / Laura — following up on Emma's ask. Quick assessment below.

Assessment summary:
- Legal: SCCs + UK IDTA + TIA mapping should cover a transient analytics processor in Canada if the following conditions are met: pseudonymisation is robust (no reversible keys), processing is strictly scoped and time-boxed, and a written attestation from the subprocessor includes: processing purpose, retention window, proof of no onward transfers, and confirmation of encryption-in-transit/storage where applicable.
- Security: require evidence of access controls and logging. For short pilots we can accept an attestation plus an on-demand evidence upload (screenshot of IAM policy + ephemeral audit export).

Proposed customer-facing artifacts:
1) subprocessor_attestation_template.pdf — one-page attestation (fields: subprocessor name, contact, scope, duration, signature).
2) TIA/DTIA mapping checklist (internal) — we use this to document how the SCC/TIA bridge applies, will share redacted copy if needed.

Operational asks for this thread:
- Aditya: ask Halcyon to send the partner contact and the pilot dates. Procurement wants attestation within 7 business days; we can meet that if Halcyon provides contact by EOD Tuesday.
- Laura: can you confirm whether portal storage is available for signed attestations? If yes we’ll confirm that as the default delivery method.

Attaching the template for review and external delivery: subprocessor_attestation_template.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
